title: React Testing Applied Check
description: Apply React testing knowledge to behavior-focused assertions, async UI, hook tests, providers, mocking strategy, flaky E2E tests, and accessibility mistakes.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A test clicks Save and immediately expects `Saved!`, but the UI updates after an async request. Which assertion style is better?

options.text: Use `await screen.findByText(/saved/i)` or `waitFor` for the async change
Assert on a private state variable

questions.explanation: Async UI should be awaited with RTL async helpers rather than fixed sleeps or implementation detail assertions.

questions.prompt: A component test uses `container.querySelector('.error')` even though the error has `role="alert"`. What query is better?
questions.explanation: Role-based queries better reflect user-facing semantics and make accessibility regressions easier to catch.

questions.prompt: A custom hook reads from context and fetches data. What may the test need? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A wrapper that provides required context
Async assertions for loading and success states

questions.explanation: Hooks with providers and async work need the same runtime environment and timing considerations as components.

questions.prompt: A test mocks the child form component, then claims the parent and form integration works. What is the risk?

options.text: The test can miss prop, callback, and accessibility issues at the integration boundary
The test will become an E2E test automatically

questions.explanation: Mocking too much can remove the behavior you meant to verify. Mock external boundaries more readily than nearby UI collaborators.

questions.prompt: A passing snapshot of a large component tree is strong proof that the user flow works correctly.
questions.explanation: Large snapshots often capture markup churn without proving meaningful behavior. User-focused assertions are usually stronger.

questions.prompt: An E2E test fails randomly because it clicks before data finishes loading. What should the test do?

options.text: Wait for a user-visible ready condition, such as a loaded row or enabled button

questions.explanation: Robust E2E tests wait for observable UI states, not arbitrary time or fragile coordinates.

questions.prompt: A form test types into an input but cannot find it by label. What product issue might the test be revealing?

options.text: The input may not be properly labeled for users and assistive technology
The test runner cannot render text inputs
The component has too many props

questions.explanation: If a test cannot find a form field by label, the UI may also be inaccessible to screen reader users.

questions.prompt: Which expectation best tests a callback prop after a user clicks Delete?
questions.explanation: For callback props, verify the observable contract: that the callback was called with the expected value after the user action.
